source_span: there are credible reasons why investors risk underestimating the scale of the tightening ahead... markets tend to underestimate, rather than overestimate the extent of hiking cycles
source_chain: The Fed (plus ECB/BoJ) has entered a new hiking cycle with markets already pricing further hikes, therefore history shows markets systematically underprice the scale of hiking cycles at the outset (1994: 140bp priced vs 300bp delivered; 2022: 200bp priced vs 400bp delivered), therefore investors today risk underestimating how much tightening is still coming, given commodity-driven inflation not yet in the data, a Fed overcorrecting for missing the last inflation wave, and looser financial conditions than in 2022 requiring more hikes to do the same work. No specific invalidation level is given; it is a base-rate/thematic argument, not a level-based call.
pulse_chain: The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% last week (unanimous), shifting the question from when cuts start to how many more hikes land, therefore futures price only 75bp more tightening by next June (DB) even though the market has guessed short before on identical terms -1994 (300bp delivered vs 140bp priced) and 2022 (400bp vs 200bp), both DB), therefore oil is now the dominant driver of the discount rate (Cboe: 10y-oil correlation at a 35-year high, +65%) so the Saudi-infrastructure oil shock feeds straight into the rate that undercuts Goldman's one-more-hike-then-flat case (built on core PCE decelerating to 2.5% annualized) because August core PCE ran hot (+0.27% m/m) despite that call, and the FOMC's reaction function has turned more hawkish (four participants want a hike at every remaining meeting) against a patience camp waiting on the labor market. Invalidation: whether the 10-year closes decisively above 5% before the October 27-28 meeting, with BTIG's Krinsky naming 4.92% as the level that flips the trend back down.
why: The pulse reproduces DB's underestimation thesis with the exact 1994/2022 figures and attribution intact, correctly represents Goldman's counter-case and its PCE basis without reversing it, and every added figure (Cboe correlation, Saudi strikes, BTIG's 4.92% level) is correctly sourced to the bank that actually said it rather than invented or misattributed.
